_about: Hand-written choices for make_curated_lineage.py. min_share: holders below it are dropped (default 0.04). drop: names removed in every snapshot. renormalise: rescale kept shares to sum to 1. notes: year -> one short sentence. Notes and sources are written from memory of the linked articles and not yet reviewed.

EGY.note: The large share held by nomads is desert west and east of the Nile, where no state governed in practice.

notes.-500: Conquered by Persia in 525 BCE (27th dynasty).
notes.-323: Taken by Alexander in 332 BCE; the Ptolemies followed.
notes.1200: Fatimid rule until 1171, then the Ayyubids; the snapshot shows the Fatimid label.
notes.1800: Ottoman province, in practice ruled by Muhammad Ali from 1805.
notes.1914: A British protectorate was declared in December 1914.

notes.400: Sasanian Empire; the snapshot labels it Persia.
notes.800: Abbasid caliphate after the Arab conquest.
notes.1500: Turkoman and Timurid successor states; the Safavids took power in 1501.

notes.-1000: Assyria in the north, Babylonia in the south.
notes.800: Seat of the Abbasid caliphate (Baghdad founded 762).
notes.1914: Ottoman provinces; a British mandate followed after the First World War.

notes.-2000: Anatolian tribes and the rise of the Hittites.
notes.1200: Byzantine Empire; the Seljuk Sultanate of Rum held the interior, which this snapshot does not show.

notes.-500: Independent city-states such as Athens and Sparta.
notes.1500: Ottoman rule; the Venetians held some islands.

notes.-500: Etruscans, Greek colonies in the south and Rome as a small republic.
notes.800: Carolingian north, Lombard duchies, the Papal States and Byzantine southern lands.
notes.1200: Fragmented between the Holy Roman Empire, the Papacy and southern kingdoms.

FRA.note: Shares are of mainland France only. The country outline also contains French Guiana (about 13 % of its area), which the automatic match labels 'Manioc farmers' and 'French Guiana'; it is left out here.

notes.-500: Gaulish (Celtic) peoples; Greek colony at Massalia.
notes.-1: Roman Gaul after Caesar's conquest (58-50 BCE).
notes.1200: Royal domain of the French kings alongside the Angevin lands and the County of Toulouse.

notes.-323: Iberian peoples with Carthaginian influence on the south coast.
notes.800: Umayyad Emirate of Cordoba; Christian Asturias in the north.
notes.1200: Almohad Caliphate in the south; Christian kingdoms of Leon, Castile, Aragon and Navarre.
notes.1500: Crowns of Castile and Aragon, united by marriage in 1469.

CHN.note: Shares are of today's territory, which includes Tibet and Xinjiang; much of that land was not under the dynasty named for China proper.

notes.-323: Warring States period; Qin was rising.
notes.400: Jin dynasty and the Sixteen Kingdoms.
notes.800: Tang dynasty and the Tibetan Empire.
notes.1200: Song dynasty with Jurchen, Liao and Xixia neighbours on the north.
notes.1914: Republic of China had replaced the Qing in 1912; the snapshot labels it Manchu Empire.

notes.-1000: Vedic period in the north, Dravidian-speaking peoples in the south.
notes.-323: Magadha (Nanda dynasty) ahead of the Mauryan Empire (from about 321 BCE).
notes.1200: Delhi Sultanate in the north; Rajput kingdoms and the Chola Empire.
notes.1800: Maratha Confederacy and many regional states beside the British East India Company.
